identity.title: exoALMA. XXIII. Estimating Disk and Planet Properties from Dust Morphologies with DBNets 2.0

paper_type_evidence.quote: We analyze the observed dust morphologies with the simulation-based inference tool DBNets2.0, assuming these are due to embedded planets at fixed locations, to infer the system properties.
we considered all fiducial Band 7 continuum observations of the exoALMA Large Program, which were CLEANed, calibrated, and made publicly available by the exoALMA collaboration

question.value: What disk properties (alpha-viscosity, scale height, dust Stokes number) and planet masses would reproduce the dust substructures of the exoALMA disks if each were carved by an embedded planet

evidence.quote: We estimate the putative planet mass, the disk $\alpha$-viscosity, scale-height, and dust Stokes number that would reproduce 19 substructures in 13 of the 15 exoALMA disks.
we aim to investigate what population of planets would be consistent with these substructures, assuming that each is the result of the disk interaction with an embedded young planet.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2021.1.01123.L.
exoALMA Band 7 ($\lambda=0.8–1.1$ mm)
we considered all fiducial Band 7 continuum observations of the exoALMA Large Program

analysis_steps.goal: select images and proposed planet locations

method.value: Use exoALMA fiducial Band 7 continuum images; choose gap and cavity locations from frank profiles of Curone et al. and the literature, excluding substructures not visible in the CLEAN radial profiles

evidence.quote: we exclude substructures that are not visible in the azimuthally averaged radial profiles obtained from the CLEANed images
we consider as viable planet locations those of gaps and cavities identified by (cite: Curone2025ExoALMA.Emission)

key_parameters.value: Cavity planets placed only where previous studies proposed planet signatures; J1842 cavity excluded from main results

evidence.quote: We select the putative planet’s location based on previous studies that proposed detections of planet signatures such as direct thermal emission or kinematic perturbations

assumptions.value: Each substructure is due to an embedded planet at the chosen fixed location

evidence.quote: assuming these are due to embedded planets at fixed locations

analysis_steps.goal: deproject and preprocess the continuum images

method.value: Deproject by linear interpolation with geometry from Curone et al., rescale to the training convention R_p = 1, crop to 0.3 R_p to 4 R_p, standardize pixel values

evidence.quote: We do that by linearly interpolating the observation and using the geometrical properties fitted by (cite: Curone2025ExoALMA.Emission).
is required as an additional input to rescale the observation to the training convention
Input observations are also standardized by subtracting the mean value of their pixels and dividing by their standard deviation
Each DBNets2.0 output considers, in principle, the entire observed morphology within $0.3R_p$ and $4R_p$, corresponding to the portion of the disk provided as input.

assumptions.value: Results unaffected by deprojection up to 60 degrees inclination, shown on synthetic data in earlier work

evidence.quote: results remain unaffected by deprojection effects up to a disk inclination of 60°

method.value: Neural posterior estimation with CNNs and normalizing flows gives the joint posterior of alpha, h, St and Mp/Mstar for each proposed planet, treated as an independent single-planet scenario

evidence.quote: DBNets2.0 uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and normalizing flows
the full joint posterior for these properties is inferred, revealing degeneracies and enabling uncertainty quantification.
we separately consider each gap as a viable planet location and independently fit our single-planet model.
All analyses and results presented here are based on $10^6$ samples drawn from each inferred posterior distribution.
The training set covers the parameter space region where $10^{-4}\leq\alpha\leq10^{-2}, 0.03\leq h \leq0.1, 10^{-3} \leq \text{St} \leq 10^{-1}, 10^{-5} \leq M_p/M_\star \leq 10^{-2}$.
This effectively sets uniform priors for each of these inferred properties in the respective range of values.

assumptions.value: Training model: 2D locally isothermal FARGO3D simulations, one non-accreting planet on a fixed orbit, constant alpha, dust as pressureless fluid with Sc=1 and fixed Stokes number, no dust back reaction

evidence.quote: One, non-accreting, planet is embedded in the disk and maintained on a fixed orbit.
Back reaction of the dust on the gas is neglected.

assumptions.value: Training images use Birnstiel et al. 2018 opacity; Gaussian noise and varying Gaussian beams added during training

evidence.quote: During training, Gaussian noise with random variance is added, and the images are convolved with Gaussian beams of varying sizes

fitting.value: Neural posterior estimation (CNN plus normalizing flow); the posterior is conditional on the training model

evidence.quote: all the inferred posteriors are to be understood as conditional upon it.

validation.value: Confidence score between 0 and 1 compares the input image with synthetic training images at samples from the posterior; CS below 0.6 flagged as uncertain, and posteriors whose 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles leave the prior support flagged as unconstrained

evidence.quote: that quantifies, with a value between 0 and 1, the similarity between the input continuum observation and the synthetic data within DBNets2.0 training sample
we adopt a conservative approach, considering estimates with CS $< 0.6$ as uncertain.
We identify as such all estimates whose 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles (corresponding to $2\sigma$ for a Gaussian) fall outside of the respective prior support.

analysis_steps.goal: convert planet-to-star mass ratio to planet mass

method.value: Multiply Mp/Mstar by dynamical stellar masses from Izquierdo et al.

evidence.quote: The conversion from $M_p/M_\star$ to $M_p$ is done using dynamical stellar masses derived by (cite: Izquierdo2025ExoALMA.Disks).

analysis_steps.goal: compare with literature planet, viscosity, aspect ratio and Stokes estimates

method.value: Compare Mp with HCI and SAM upper limits, kinematic and gap-width estimates; compare alpha with line-broadening turbulence; compare h with temperature-derived aspect ratios under vertical hydrostatic equilibrium; compare with the earlier DBNets2.0 sample

evidence.quote: Figure [2](#fig:litmp) presents a comparison of our planet mass estimates with the literature.
can be compared to our estimates of the disks’ aspect ratios by converting them under the assumption of vertical hydrostatic equilibrium.

validation.value: Estimates are mostly consistent with HCI upper limits except J1604 and LkCa 15; Band 7 results agree within uncertainties with the earlier Band 6 and Band 3 DBNets2.0 results

evidence.quote: We found our estimates to be mostly consistent with these constraints, with the only two exceptions of J1604 and LkCa15 for which we estimate higher planet masses.
estimates are compatible within uncertainties, proving little dependence of these results on the Band of the observations.

analysis_steps.goal: derive implications for accretion, migration, stability and correlations

method.value: Compute local alpha h^2 and compare with accretion timescales; compute Kanagawa K and K' against migration thresholds; check Hill stability of the six two-planet systems; compute Pearson correlations with other disk properties

evidence.quote: Conversely, with DBNets2.0, we can provide local estimates of $\alpha h^2$ obtained by modelling substructures due to planet-disk interaction
This is required to be greater than $2\sqrt{3}$ for the system to be stable.
we computed the Pearson correlation coefficient ($\rho$)

key_parameters.value: Significance threshold p < 0.05; uncertain and unconstrained estimates removed from the correlation analysis

evidence.quote: A p-value lower than 0.05 indicates statistical significant evidence for correlation between the two properties.
For this analysis, we remove all estimates that we considered either unreliable or unconstrained.

assumptions.value: Self-similar disk evolution assumed for the accretion timescale relation

evidence.quote: assuming the self-similar solution to the disk evolution

used_for.value: Simulation-based inference of planet mass, alpha, h and St from dust continuum images

evidence.quote: DBNets2.0 is a simulation-based inference pipeline for rapidly fitting dust substructures, such as gaps, rings and cavities, observed in disks’ dust continuum emission.

used_for.value: Hydrodynamical simulations that generate the DBNets2.0 training set

evidence.quote: Hydrodynamical simulations are run with the mesh code FARGO3D

used_for.value: Azimuthally symmetric radial profile fits of the continuum, used (via Curone et al.) to locate gaps and cavities

evidence.quote: through the characterization of the azimuthally symmetric `frank` (cite: Jennings2020Frankenstein:Process) fits of the disks’ continuum emission

results_numeric.quantity: Number of putative planets and disks with DBNets2.0 estimates

evidence.quote: we propose a population of 19 planets possibly embedded in 13 of the 15 disks targeted by the exoALMA program

results_numeric.quantity: alpha for the 72 au gap in DM Tau

evidence.quote: The analysis of the gap at 72 au instead returns an estimate $\alpha=5.5^{+3.1}_{-2.0} \times 10^{-3}$

results_numeric.quantity: log St for the 86 au gap in LkCa 15

evidence.quote: we estimate $\log \text{St} = -1.45^{+0.12}_{-0.14}$

results_numeric.value: 3 (inner gap of MWC 758, cavities of HD 135344 B and LkCa 15)

evidence.quote: These are three estimates for putative planets in the inner gap of MWC 758 and in the cavities of HD 135344 B and LkCa 15.

results_numeric.quantity: Putative planets expected to migrate outward

evidence.quote: most of our planets would fall into the inward migrating case, with only three objects migrating outwards.

results_numeric.quantity: Pearson correlation, stellar mass versus inferred aspect ratio

evidence.quote: Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.60

findings_qualitative.value: Inferred alpha distribution has two peaks at the two ends of the prior, with more sources at low viscosity

evidence.quote: with an higher number of sources showing evidence of low viscosity

findings_qualitative.value: Cavities suggest more massive companions than gaps

evidence.quote: Cavities are found to suggest the presence of more massive companions

findings_qualitative.value: All six proposed two-planet systems would be dynamically stable and not in low-order mean-motion resonances

evidence.quote: all these systems would be dynamically stable and are not close enough to lie in the lower-order mean-motion resonances

findings_qualitative.value: Inferred planet mass depends on assumed location inside cavities and decreases as the planet nears the outer ring

evidence.quote: the inferred planet mass decreases as the assumed planet location approaches the ring.

claims.hypothesis: Do the exoALMA dust substructures, if planet-carved, imply planet masses consistent with other constraints
claims.experiment: Applied DBNets2.0 to Band 7 continuum images at proposed planet locations and compared with HCI limits, kinematic and empirical estimates
claims.result: Most estimates consistent with HCI upper limits and simulation or empirical estimates; J1604 and LkCa 15 cavity planets are more massive than previous constraints; planets in HD 34282 and J1604 are the best direct-imaging candidates
claims.finding: Most proposed planets are super-Jovian (likely selection bias) and cavities require larger masses than gaps

evidence.quote: Most of our estimates are consistent with upper limits set by high-contrast imaging and estimates from simulations or empirical formulae.
Most of the proposed planets are super-Jovian, likely due to sample selection bias.

claims.hypothesis: Can viscous transport inferred from planet-disk substructures explain observed stellar accretion rates
claims.experiment: Compared local alpha h^2 from DBNets2.0 with global accretion timescales from rotation-curve modelling
claims.result: Viscous timescales are too long for all Herbig stars; T Tauri stars show larger scatter, mostly roughly consistent
claims.finding: Additional accretion mechanisms are needed for the Herbig stars

evidence.quote: for all the Herbig stars in our sample, our measure of the disk timescale for viscous transport cannot explain the observed accretion rate

claims.hypothesis: Which migration regime do the proposed planets occupy
claims.experiment: Computed Kanagawa K and K' from DBNets2.0 estimates and compared with outward-migration thresholds
claims.result: Most planets fall in the inward-migration regime; three objects migrate outward

evidence.quote: most of our planets would fall into the inward migrating case, with only three objects migrating outwards.

claims.hypothesis: Do inferred disk and planet properties correlate with other disk properties
claims.experiment: Pearson correlations with gas-to-dust ratio, non-axisymmetry index, gas, dust and stellar masses
claims.result: Only stellar mass versus aspect ratio is significant (Pearson coefficient 0.60)

evidence.quote: We do not observe any statistically significant correlation, with the sole exception of the pair stellar mass-aspect ratio

claims.hypothesis: Do DBNets2.0 estimates depend on observing band
claims.experiment: Compared Band 7 exoALMA estimates with earlier Band 6 and Band 3 DBNets2.0 estimates for overlapping objects
claims.result: Planet masses compatible within uncertainties; alpha for DM Tau differs by more than one order of magnitude at Band 3
claims.finding: alpha and St estimates should not be fully trusted at wavelengths far from Band 6

evidence.quote: we should not fully trust DBNets2.0 estimates on $\alpha$ and St when those are inferred using observations at wavelengths significantly different than those of Band 6.

why_this_data.value: exoALMA provides a homogeneous sample of dust continuum observations with substructures in nearly all disks

evidence.quote: represent a rare and valuable case of a homogenous sample

why_this_method.value: Machine-learning SBI combines the speed of empirical relations with the expressiveness of neural networks and uses the whole observed morphology

evidence.quote: combining the same speed and ease of use of empirical relations with the higher expressiveness of neural networks

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: J1842 cavity excluded from the main results because no planet-signature constraints exist; results shown as a function of assumed planet location

evidence.quote: exclude from our main discussions the cavity of J1842, which lacks such constraints

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Estimates with CS below 0.6 or unconstrained posteriors excluded from aggregated results

evidence.quote: We exclude these points from the presentation and discussion of aggregated results

limitations_admitted.value: Posteriors are conditional on the training model and cannot capture scenarios outside it

evidence.quote: The inferred distributions cannot account for scenarios that are not included in this model.

limitations_admitted.value: Planet migration is not modelled because planets are held on fixed orbits

evidence.quote: does not include planet migration, as planets are held on a fixed orbit.

limitations_admitted.value: exoALMA sample is biased toward brighter and more extended disks

evidence.quote: the exoALMA sample is inherently affected by selection biases, leading to an overrepresentation of brighter and more extended disks

limitations_admitted.value: Prior upper limit alpha<=1e-2 is too constraining for DM Tau

evidence.quote: DBNets2.0 priors are too constraining in this case

referee_caveats_inferred: Planet locations are chosen by hand and, for cavities, strongly drive the inferred mass; results are scenario-dependent
Each substructure is fitted independently with a single-planet model, so multi-planet inferences rest on an untested assumption
Training uses 2D locally isothermal simulations with a single grain size and a fixed Band 6 opacity setup, so alpha and St are model-dependent and band-sensitive
No test that the data are better described by planets than by non-planetary substructure mechanisms

evidence.quote: made publicly available by the exoALMA collaboration

missing_for_reproduction: Trained DBNets2.0 model and inference code access
Exact exoALMA image files and per-disk deprojection geometry
Training-set generation and network details beyond the appendix summary
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Small: 15 Band 7 continuum images (about tens of MB total) from the released exoALMA products; no visibility processing needed
reproducibility.score_reason: Public images, planet radii and numeric result tables are given, but the inference depends on the DBNets2.0 trained model from earlier papers and on preprocessing details not listed here.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Recipe depends on a pretrained external tool and on inputs defined in companion papers, so it cannot be redone from this paper alone.
